How is it pushing you to complete your own odyssey? That's the question Seneca says we should be asking about the odyssey. Not what happened to Odysseus, but what is this story asking of me and am I answering? What is life asking of me and am I answering? He thinks that this is the story that's supposed to help us slay our own monsters, sail through our own storms, get back to our own Ithaca. That's what the Odyssey is all about. That's what people keep missing.
